docs.place.component: THE PLACE: a chair and an avatar — the seat design, as the desks add-on ships it. Both are drawn by `@game-presets/desks` and the kit's own presence, one source for every desk on the shelf.

A container. It stands on the felt, turned to the desk, carries a hand and its rights. It exists by itself: a place may be held while its player is looking at the far end of the room. It is the design's ARCH — a half-round front into the desk, a flat back at the owner — in a black keyline with the place's own ink as the rim inside it. Parameters: position · angle · the place's colour (`spin`) · the hand and its pose (three toggles: fan · shrink · tuck) · pin · lock · hide · mine or somebody's.

The state of a player's camera: a disc, a cone of the look, a name, a ring while the hand is full. The cone is built into the disc — its apex is the disc's centre — so it cannot come apart. Parameters: name · where it looks · state (in the chair · adrift · not looking) · a full hand.

The avatar IN the chair: the disc in the arch, the look along the place's angle. The avatar OFF the chair: the place stays held and coloured, the avatar slides the way it is looking. A place without an avatar is a dashed outline: one may sit down. The chair, the hand and the cone inherit the angle. The name and its plate — never.
## Rights are marks, controls are on the glass

Pin, lock and hide are badges in a column on the owner's left of the arch, up only while the state is on — so the whole table reads why a card will not come out before anybody reaches for it. The controls that turn them are on the owner's own screen, at the foot of the glass: the rights on the left, the hand's fold on the right (`Live/Hands`).
docs.place.sample: One place under every knob the design has. Turn the chair, pick its colour, deal it a hand and choose the pose; put the avatar in it, slide it off, take its look away; switch the rights on and watch the marks stand up beside the arch. `mine` puts the gold ring outside the keyline.
docs.place.avatars: 1 · THE AVATAR WITHOUT A CHAIR. A disc, a cone of the look, a name, a ring for a full hand. The avatar knows nothing about furniture and nothing about cards. Looking at the desk; looking aside (the direction is its own parameter, and the cone is part of the disc: its apex at the centre); a full hand (a ring round the disc, seen from across the table); not looking (no cone at all: the player's camera is not on this desk).
docs.place.chairs: 2 · THE CHAIR WITHOUT AN AVATAR. A place: angle, the player's colour, the hand, the rights. The player may not be at the screen, and the place stays theirs. Empty — dashed and nobody's: one may sit down. Held — the rim in the player's ink, and a place is held without a card. Then the hand in the eight poses three toggles make — fan (the angle: a ladder on the owner's right, or an arc in front of the arch), shrink (the distance: a stack beside, the arc closed to a sliver in front), tuck (the height: under the chair with a tip past the rim) — one at a time and combined; open — the cards face up, the player has shown the table their hand; part open — a flip of single cards. Mine: the same colour as everybody's, with the gold ring outside — "this is me". Pin, lock, hide, and all three at once: the marks stack in a column on the left. Turned: the chair and the hand inherit the angle.
docs.place.together: 3 · TOGETHER. The avatar sits in the chair: the disc in the arch, the look along the place's angle, the hand at the rim. Gone — the place stays held, the avatar slides the way it is looking. Not looking here — the chair is held, the hand is in place, no cone. Mine with rights: the gold ring outside the keyline, the marks beside the arch. And fifty-two cards: a stack holds its thickness and does not grow into a ladder; a fan holds its arc and its width, the step closes up; open, the same arc face up.
docs.place.ring: PLACES ROUND THE DESK. The angle comes from the position on the rim: the cone always into the felt, the stack on the owner's right, the names always upright. The same arithmetic seats every live desk on the shelf (`roundPlaces`).
